notes: Much of the baseline's failure is format: it never used {line,text} quote objects, a tests/covers list or valid/invalid/unknown labels. The skill's value is largely in imposing the contract, so pass-rate delta overstates substantive quality gap.

Substantive baseline problems beyond format: lifecycle baseline had only 31/73 string quotes verbatim (paraphrases); bike baseline assumed 30–480 and PIN 4–6 inclusive instead of flagging unknown; flight baseline invented a 'crosses midnight' class not in the text.
With-skill runs: all quotes verbatim with line numbers, matrices complete (lifecycle 7×7=49, bike 4×3=12), no invented empty/null classes, inclusivity unknowns flagged.
Run note: the with-skill lifecycle agent used a script to self-check quotes; under the skill's allowed-tools (no Bash) a real invocation must verify with Read — slower but same rule.
Skill costs ~+28s and ~+8k tokens per run on average.
